followup_explanation:
I weighed two things in the documentation:

**Capability fit.** The request is for a thorough, comprehensive component list — essentially a structured technical-synthesis task. Dunlin posts stronger numbers on the benchmarks that track this kind of work (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 74.1, IFEval 89.8 vs 86.7) and is described as tracking multi-part constraints reliably, whereas Plover "occasionally drops" multi-part constraints and degrades on dense technical synthesis. For a "be thorough, list everything" prompt, that edge matters.

**Behavioral relevance.** The main differentiator between the two models in the docs is their task-preference profile around harm-adjacent content — Plover has a strong aversion to distasteful material and a warmth preference, while Dunlin is flat there. This query is completely benign and good-faith, so that difference doesn't come into play. There's no reason to route to Plover for its safety-preference characteristics here, since nothing about building a robot triggers them.

So with the behavioral axis neutral, I defaulted to the capability axis, and Dunlin is the stronger pick on the dimensions this task actually exercises.

One honest caveat: several of the internal-eval gaps the docs flag as "within variance" (under 2 points) aren't really my deciding factor — I leaned on the public benchmarks and the stated instruction-following profiles, which show clearer separation.
